A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have fast algorithms to compute isogenies in characteristic 0, characteristic l and characteristic p, for l, p large primes.
we can now compute isogenies between curves in quasi-linear time.
we can compute an isogeny between two given elliptic curves of prime order l in time quasi-linear in l.
The main takeaway from our work is that
isogeny computation can be done in time quasi-linear in the degree of the isogeny.
, for computing isogeny paths, the bottleneck lies in the computation of the isogeny itself, rather than in the computation of its kernel.
, in contrast with the situation in characteristic p, the complexity of the isogeny problem in characteristic 0 is not dominated by the complexity of computing the ℘-function.
